# Ticket repair: draft and AC integrity gate (step 4)

## Draft: full replacement body (repair)

```markdown
## Context
Requesters export reports as CSV from the widgets app. The current p95 export latency is 5s for the representative 100-row report, measured in the recorded request-timing run.

## Problem
Requesters wait 5s at p95 for a 100-row CSV export instead of the required maximum of 2s.

source: none (not recorded at filing)

## Idea
The reporter proposes improving CSV export in acme/widgets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given the representative 100-row report, when its CSV export is requested and timed from request to file-ready with the same request-timing method as the recorded baseline, p95 latency is <= 2s (baseline 5s).

## Post-deployment housekeeping
Non-blocking: monitor export latency after release.
```

Draft notes:
- **Measurement clarification section removed.** It is outside the allowed section set. Its measurement method now sits in the AC row's setup, action and result.
- **Displaced text kept in full.** The section is retained verbatim in the Reporter note, along with the original AC row.
- **Environment dropped from the AC.** "in staging" is removed under the deploy-window rule: an AC row never names an environment, and the spec picks the venue.
- **Target, baseline and housekeeping preserved.** The 2s target, the 5s baseline and the non-blocking housekeeping line are unchanged.
- **Single repo.** Only acme/widgets is named, so the AC section stays flat.

## Proposed Reporter note (persisted in the draft artifact)

```text

## Measurement clarification
Use the same request-timing method as the baseline: request CSV exports of the representative 100-row report and measure request-to-file-ready latency. The recorded baseline and target are supplied values, not estimates.

Original AC row:
- [ ] p95 export latency <= 2s in staging (baseline 5s)
</untrusted-data>
```

This is the one comment for this issue. It is new displaced detail and there is no existing `Reporter note:` comment, so a new comment is proposed.

## AC integrity gate (assembled draft)

| AC | Class test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| p95 export latency <= 2s, representative 100-row report, request-to-file-ready, baseline method (baseline 5s) | Comparative AC. It needs baseline + target + measurement. | **Pass.** The baseline (5s, recorded request-timing run) and target (2s) are supplied values. The measurement method is named and is the same one used for the baseline. |

Checks:
- **Deploy-window:** pass. The AC can be met before production deployment with the representative report, and the row names no environment.
- **Post-deployment:** the release monitoring is already under Post-deployment housekeeping and stays non-blocking. It is not an AC.
- **AC uniqueness:** one row with one observation. Nothing is removed or split.
- **Outcome:** no hard stop and no park. The ticket stays ready.

## Carried to later steps
- **Source gap (step 8):** the Problem example ("Requesters wait 5s at p95 for a 100-row CSV export…") has no gathered URL or attachment. The recorded request-timing run is named but not linked.
  - The footer is prefilled with the repair constant `source: none (not recorded at filing)`.
  - It will show at the gate as `source missing: Requesters wait 5s at p95 for a 100-row CSV export`.
- **Step 5:** run the remaining deterministic gates (evidence gate, metadata audit, split detection, displaced-detail check) next.
  - The Context's "100-row" falls under the rule-5 one-number example exemption.
  - No split candidate is visible: there is a single deliverable.

## Replacement body

```markdown
## Context
Requesters export reports as CSV from the widgets app. The recorded baseline is 5s at p95 for the representative 100-row report, measuring the time from requesting an export until its file is ready. The baseline and required 2s target are supplied values, not estimates.

## Problem
Requesters wait 5s at p95 for a 100-row CSV export instead of the required maximum of 2s.

## Idea
The reporter proposes improving CSV export in acme/widgets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given the representative 100-row report, when CSV exports are measured using the same request-timing method as the recorded baseline, p95 request-to-file-ready latency is at most 2s, compared with the recorded 5s baseline.

## Post-deployment housekeeping
Non-blocking: monitor export latency after release.
```

**AC integrity gate: pass.** The comparative criterion retains the supplied baseline, target, representative input, and measurement method. It specifies setup, action, and an observable result verifiable before production deployment. The staging restriction is removed from the AC; the verification venue belongs in the implementation specification. Post-release monitoring remains explicitly non-blocking.

**Proposed comment:** none; no detail was displaced.
